analysis_runs.notes: Dependency-collapsed systemic ACH over verified detention guarantee/utilization findings. Created verified medium synthesis #13032; assessed #13032 neutral to H1 #335 and consistent with H0 #336. No new hypothesis or lead; no external queries.

Zero new hunches after novelty and dependency gates. Surge readiness is already H0 #336; adaptive minimum and floor-plus-surge candidates lack three independent period-compatible contexts and current rate/invoice evidence. No external queries and no auto_leads.

finding_records.summary: DHS OIG reported that ICE paid approximately $25.3 million for unused bed space at Golden State Annex during the preceding 12 months.
Oversight.gov currently marks OIG-24-23 recommendation 7, requiring ICE to update the Golden State guaranteed minimum, as closed.
DHS OIG found ICE attempted to impose staffing penalties through 2019 and 2021 discrepancy reports but did not enforce them, while Folkston received full contract funding.
In its response to OIG-22-47, ICE said Folkston was covering all posts with overtime at the vendor's expense while applicants cleared; Oversight.gov now marks the staffing recommendation closed.
Signed Folkston IGSA modification P00022 lists a performance period ending February 15, 2027.

As a non-GEO comparator, ICE was assessing a 25 percent reduction in Torrance monthly billing as a staffing penalty and cut the guaranteed minimum from 714 detainees to 505 because of continued staffing problems.

finding_records.target_name: The GEO Group FY2025 ICE activation wave
finding_records.summary: GEO disclosed a sequence of FY2025 ICE activations: Delaney Hall awarded February 27, North Lake announced for immediate activation March 20, and D. Ray James activated under a contract modification effective June 6.
GEO’s Tacoma ICE facility contract carried a $700 million ten-year minimum, while facility gross profit was $18.6-$23.5 million annually in 2010-2018.
ICE contract 70CDCR20D00000008 set Golden State CLIN 0003A’s guaranteed minimum at 560 beds and listed 204,400 bed-days for December 20, 2022 through December 19, 2023.
DHS OIG measured Golden State’s average daily detainee population at 136 from April 20, 2022 through April 19, 2023.
ICE contract 70CDCR20D00000009 set Adelanto’s guaranteed-minimum tier at 1,455 beds and listed 531,075 bed-days for ordinary contract years.
ICE contract 70CDCR20D00000009 set Desert View’s guaranteed-minimum tier at 600 beds and listed 219,000 bed-days for ordinary contract years.
At the January 2012 ICE inspection, Tacoma had 1,579 beds and housed 1,358 ICE detainees.

finding_records.target_name: Folkston ICE Processing Center and Annex
finding_records.summary: DHS OIG reported FY2021 ADP/capacity of 286/780 at Folkston IPC and 88/338 at Folkston Annex.
DHS OIG reported fixed monthly minimum charges of $1,993,449.32, then $2,043,182.40, and $1,930,957.98 after Torrance’s minimum fell to 505 in January 2022.
The reviewed Aurora contract bundle contains a minimum-quantity bed-day CLIN, but redacts the number of beds, rate, and amount.
The reviewed Aurora contract bundle contains a monthly flat fixed transportation fee whose rate and amount are redacted.
ICE ODO’s July 2024 Adelanto follow-up reported no findings.
DHS OIG closed its South Texas housing-requirements recommendation after ICE said it would combine housing units to meet the contract's guaranteed minimum while following COVID-19 protocols.

DHS OIG kept Northwest recommendation 7 unresolved and open after ICE declined to update the contract's guaranteed minimum; OIG said closure required historical-needs analysis and an appropriate adjustment.
USAspending describes Denver task-order modification P00011 as increasing the maximum number of beds and obligating additional funding.
USAspending describes South Texas task-order modification P00001 as incorporating emergency beds.
ICE ODO found two repeat deficiencies in its August 2024 Northwest follow-up after the facility completed its January 2024 UCAP, which ODO said may not have been sufficient to prevent them.
USAspending describes Northwest task-order modification P00008 as extending the task-order term and adding funding for detention, transportation, expansion, remote-post, and overtime-bed services.

Across 78 GEO-linked ICE inspection events, 42 of the 58 events in the compliant-grade family separately reported deficient components; 12 explicitly reported zero deficient components and four left component status unstated or ambiguous.

Funding-only and initial new/base task actions accounted for 98.3474% of FY2025 net obligations and 85.6478% of FY2026-through-July-9 net obligations; only one ICE action in scope was an explicit option exercise, the $11,894,500 Tacoma FY2025 modification.

Net obligations were 25.1369% higher in FY2026 through July 9 than in the FY2025 same-elapsed window; $262,845,644.26, or 40.5324% of FY2026-to-date net, clustered from January 21 through January 28 across seven facility/service categories.

Gross deobligations were $7,062,337.49 in FY2025 and $3,004,649.21 in FY2026 through July 9, only 0.8625% and 0.4612% of gross positive obligations; they reduce net totals rather than explain the positive acceleration.
Retrieved current ICE modifications preserve bed-day, guarantee and staffing-plan fields but redact the values needed for a like-for-like historical rate comparison.
DHS OIG reported a South Texas guaranteed minimum of 1,350 detainees at $100.86 per detainee-day, increasing to $101.36 in August 2021.
DHS OIG found 36 percent of South Texas guaranteed bed space was unused on average from November 2020 through October 2021 and that ICE paid approximately $18 million for unused bed space.
USAspending records $60,523,845.63 obligated and $60,523,865.31 in outlays for completed South Texas task order 70CDCR24FR0000038, whose performance period was August 6, 2024 through August 5, 2025.
South Texas task-order closeout modification P00009 deobligated $529,091.27 as excess funding on November 14, 2025.

finding_records.target_name: Western GEO CDF guarantee utilization shift
finding_records.summary: TIER 2 SYNTHESIS: A dependency-collapsed ICE FY25/FY26 YTD comparison shows all four Western GEO CDFs above reported minimums by 2026-04-02 after Adelanto, Desert View, and Tacoma were below or nearly at them on 2025-09-15; the shift coincides with enforcement expansion but does not prove historical unused-bed payments were cost-effective or financially remedied.

new_assessments.notes: Dependency-collapsed FY25/FY26 YTD utilization shift does not reveal current rates, billed bed-days, invoices, deductions, prior forecasts, or whether financial consequences tracked utilization. Later high use is compatible with insulation and therefore does not discriminate against H1.

Later above-minimum utilization across the shared four-facility snapshot is consistent with surge-readiness capacity becoming used during enforcement expansion. It does not establish that prior unused-bed payments were forecast-based or cost-effective, so this is limited support, not confirmation.
